newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Merrill Lynch charges ex-employee with cheating.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch charges ex-employee with cheating.

text.p: U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch said on Friday it had filed charges in Singapore and Hong Kong against a former Singapore employee on suspicion of fraud.
A Merrill Lynch spokesman told Reuters from Hong Kong that the company had started civil proceedings against the man, who was fired last month.
The spokesman declined to comment on the amount in question. Singapore state television quoted industry sources as estimating some US$30 million was involved.
The accused man was a former private client financial consultant based in Singapore, the spokesman said.
In its statement of claim, the company said the former employee "...has engaged in unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures."
The spokesman said Merrill Lynch had filed a criminal complaint in Singapore and was working closely with the relevant regulatory authorities.
Merrill Lynch has also sought to freeze the man's assets internationally and prevent their dissipation.
The former employee had been in Hong Kong recently but his whereabouts were not known, the spokesman said.
